newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken no comment on Nordbanken merger.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken no comment on Nordbanken merger.

text.p: Swedish bank S-E-Banken had no further comments on Monday about failed merger discussions with rival Nordbanken after a Swedish newspaper reported the head of Nordbanken saying a merger would be good.
"No discussions are going on at the moment," S-E-Banken spokeswoman Annika Halldin told Reuters. "We do not have any additional comments."

The banks' merger talks failed at the beginning of February. No reason for the collapse in talks was given but market players speculated that it was over a disagreement on management of a merged bank.
Halldin reiterated that S-E-Banken had withdrawn from merger talks as the deal did not look good enough for its shareholders and customers.
Nordbanken's chief executive Hans Dalborg said in a Monday newspaper article in Sweden's Dagens Nyheter that a merger would be good, but said no talks were going on at the moment.
"We still think that a merger with S-E-Banken is a good idea," Dalborg was quoted as saying.
"From Nordbanken's point of view we thought negotiations were constructive and nice and that a deal would be good for shareholders, customers and others. We still have that vision."
Analysts last week said merger talks could resume after Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced a merger and Handelsbanken finalised its 23 billion crown bid for Stadshypotek.
On the Stockholm Stock Exchange, the banks' shares advanced at 1000 GMT with S-E-Banken up one crown at 83 and Nordbanken gaining two to 265 but off a morning high of 269 crowns.
